chunks: With this chain, from al-Husayn, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites 'Glory be to the Name of your Lord, the Most High' in an obligatory or recommended prayer, it will be said to him on the Day of Judgment: Enter Paradise from whichever door you wish, if God wills.

key_terms.سُبُّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى: Glory be to the Name of your Lord, the Most High (Surah Al-A'la, Quran 87:1)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-A'la in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* via the chain of Abu Basir, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the immense virtue of reciting Surah al-A'la, linking it directly to the concept of 'Tasbih al-A'la' (Glory to the Most High). The promise of choosing one's own gate into Paradise signifies a unique honor and elevated status for the believer, reflecting the Surah's thematic focus on the inevitability of the Hereafter and the purification of the soul.
